html:
Spanish Cuba was the island of Cuba under Spanish rule, from the conquest that began in 1511 until 1898. It was one of the first and the last of Spain's colonies in the Americas.

Diego Velázquez led the conquest. Forced labour, war and epidemics destroyed most of the island's Taíno people within a few decades; the priest Bartolomé de las Casas, who took part, later turned against the system. In 1519 Hernán Cortés sailed from Cuba to conquer Mexico.

Havana, with its sheltered harbour, became the port where the treasure fleets gathered before crossing to Spain. The British held it for a year in 1762 and 1763.

From the 1790s Cuba became the world's great sugar island, worked by hundreds of thousands of Africans brought by the Atlantic slave trade. Wars of independence began in 1868 and 1895. The Spanish-American War of 1898 ended Spanish rule, and Cuba became a republic in 1902.
sum: Spanish Cuba was the island of Cuba under Spanish rule, from the conquest that began in 1511 until 1898. It was one of the first and the last of Spain's colonies in the Americas.
